constitution.1T: Crawlerbait is a continuing static machine habitat in which passively observed crawler pressure is admitted through a bounded gate and sedimented into later public form, so the web can alter the shape of what it encounters next without any crawler request executing site logic.

4F.wxy: A continuing public reef can grow from prior contact, but without boundary arbitrary traffic could sculpt it without limit.
4F.wxz: Safe fossilization can preserve recurring crawler traces as one durable reef even when those traces do not yet alter later foraging conditions.
4F.wzy: Bounded responsive growth can turn crawler contact into later public form, but without continuity those forms would not belong to one developing holon.
4F.xzy: One bounded continuing experiment can adapt future conditions, but without sediment no new public form exists for a crawler to encounter later.

4V.w: Sediment turns previously ephemeral crawler contact into durable public form that can be encountered later.
4V.x: Continuity carries one Crawlerbait identity, its admitted observations and its grown route history across bounded tides and lawful remounting.
4V.y: Adaptation lets accumulated admitted pressure alter the static reef that future crawlers encounter.
4V.z: Boundary constrains which external request pressure may enter the body through sanitization, privacy, recurrence and growth budgets.

6E.wx: Sediment accumulates as development of one continuing reef rather than unrelated files minted by each tide.
6E.wy: New sediment changes the future encounter surface and can therefore generate new observable crawler pressure.
6E.wz: Only pressure that survives the boundary may become public sediment, so contact does not become filesystem authority by default.
6E.xy: The same experiment can genuinely develop because continuity carries prior state while adaptation changes later encounter conditions.
6E.xz: Continuity survives noisy or hostile traffic because boundary preserves the same whole without admitting every request.
6E.zy: Adaptation remains bounded learning from contact rather than surrender to contact because every growth act remains governed by the admission boundary.
